summary: This Wikipedia article gives an overview of Boston, Massachusetts, covering its schools, sports teams and parks, television market, colleges, economy, neighborhoods and immigrant communities, climate, medical facilities, government, and history from the Puritan founding onward. It describes Boston as the state capital and largest city in New England, with a large tourism and education economy and a strong cultural and literary heritage. The note also covers the city's transportation and commuting trends, its LGBT press, and its political representation at federal and municipal levels.
one_line: Overview of Boston, Massachusetts: its schools, sports, parks, economy, demographics, climate, government and history.
key_facts: Boston Public Schools enrolls 57,000 students attending 145 schools.
Boston Latin School, established 1635, is the oldest public high school in the US.
The Boston Red Sox play their home games at Fenway Park, built in 1912.
Boston was the site of the first game of the first modern World Series, in 1903.
Boston Common is the oldest public park in the United States.
The Boston Public Library was founded in 1852 as the first free library in the United States.
People of Irish descent form the largest single ethnic group in the city, at 15.8% of the population.
The city averages 43.8 inches (1,110 mm) of precipitation a year.
Boston has won 36 championships in major North American professional leagues, as of 2014.
The Greater Boston metropolitan area has the sixth-largest economy in the country, encompassing $363 billion.
The city proper covers 48 square miles (124 km2) with an estimated population of 655,884 in 2014.
Marty Walsh became Mayor in January 2014, succeeding Thomas Menino, whose twenty-year tenure was the longest in the city's history.
Tourism brought 21.2 million domestic and international visitors spending $8.3 billion in 2011.
Boston was ranked 36th worldwide in quality of living in a 2011 survey of 221 major cities.
Boston Latin School and America's first public school were both founded in Boston in 1635.
